transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... it's about my husband's sister. She’s been working this whole family business thing just so she can get control of the money. She's trying to push me completely out of making any decisions. And, well, no matter how folks try to smooth it over or tell me otherwise, I know what I’ve been seeing. It's been going on for more than a year now, plain as day.
Have you ever felt like you were hearing things that others around you couldn't hear, or that you were receiving special messages meant only for you?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or anything, and I'm not getting secret messages. I just see what she's doing right in front of me. It's not in my head, it's just... what's happening with the business and the money. I don't need special messages to see that she's trying to push me out.
Do you find that you feel this same level of suspicion and mistrust toward other people in your life, such as friends, coworkers, or even other family members?

No, not at all. I get along fine with my friends, and... well, the rest of the family is okay. I don't go around thinking everybody is out to get me or anything like that. 

It's really just her. I only don't trust her because of what she's actually doing with the money. With everyone else, I'm just my normal self. I trust people just fine when they aren't trying to steal from us.
Can you tell me about the specific evidence or actions you've seen that make you certain she is trying to steal the money?

Well... I don't have, like, paperwork or bank statements to show you, if that's what you mean. I haven't gone digging through the books or anything like that. 

It's just... I can just tell by the way she acts around me when the money or the business comes up. You just know when someone is working against you. I don't really have a specific list of things to give you, or hard proof I can hand over. I just know what I'm seeing.
How has this situation with your sister-in-law affected your ability to go about your daily routine or maintain your usual responsibilities?

It hasn't really stopped me from doing what I need to do. I still keep up with my quilting group and choir practice, and I'm still going to my GED lessons and doing my senior walks just like I always have. 

It hasn't ruined my whole life or anything. Mostly, it's just changed how much I trust my husband's sister. I just have to be careful about which family gatherings I feel comfortable going to now, because I don't want to be around her if I can help it. But other than that, my day-to-day routine is pretty much the same.
Have you ever talked to your husband about these suspicions regarding his sister, and if so, what does he say about it?

I haven't really brought it up with him. I mean, I've thought about it, but... it's his sister, you know? I just don't know how he'd take it. I don't want to start a big fight between him and his family if I don't have to. So, no, I've just kept it to myself for now.
Are there any other beliefs or concerns you hold that your husband or other family members might disagree with or think are not based on reality?

No, not really. I mean, it's just this thing with his sister. I don't have any other big secrets or... or strange ideas that people would think are crazy. It's just her, and what I know she's doing. Everything else in my life is pretty normal.
Are there any ideas or hunches you have that you've kept to yourself because you suspect other people might think they sound strange or impossible?

No, like I was just saying, I really don't. I don't have any other... strange hunches or anything impossible like that. It's strictly just what I know about his sister. I don't have anything else I'm keeping secret from people because it sounds weird. It's just that one situation, and the rest of my life is just regular day-to-day stuff.
Do you believe that anyone else, perhaps other family members or business associates, is working alongside your sister-in-law to help her take control of the money?

No, I don't think so. I haven't seen anything that makes me think anyone else is involved. It's really just her. I think she's doing it all on her own. I haven't noticed anyone else acting strange or... or trying to get involved with the money. So, no, just her.
Have you noticed any changes in your personality or how you interact with people generally over the last few years, even outside of this situation with your sister-in-law?

No, not really. I mean, my day-to-day life is exactly the same as it's always been. I still go to my quilting group, and choir practice... I'm still taking my GED lessons, and doing my senior walks. All of that is normal. The only thing that's changed is, well, how much I trust his sister. And... I guess I'm a lot more careful about which family gatherings I go to now, because I just don't feel comfortable being around her. But outside of that, I'm the same person I've always been.

When you are around your sister-in-law, do you ever feel like she is trying to communicate something to you through non-verbal cues, such as specific gestures, the way she moves, or the way she looks at you, that others might not notice?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. She doesn't make any secret gestures or give me weird looks. I mean, to my face, she acts pretty normal, honestly. She's just polite and smiles like everything is fine. She's not trying to send me any hidden messages or anything like that. All the stuff she's doing with the money is behind the scenes, so... no, she just acts like her usual self when we happen to be in the same room.
Do you feel that your sister-in-law's actions go beyond just the business and money, and that she might actually be trying to physically hurt you or put your safety at risk?

No, no, I don't think she wants to hurt me physically. It's nothing like that. I don't feel like my safety is at risk or anything. It's really just about the money and the business. She wants control of the finances, but I don't think she'd ever try to actually harm me.

If your husband were to show you bank statements or financial records that proved your sister-in-law was not taking any money, would you be willing to accept that as proof, or would you still believe she is finding ways to hide it?

Honestly... no, I wouldn't accept that as proof. Papers can be faked, or she could just be hiding things off the books. I came in here today because my husband’s sister has been working this family business specifically so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over, or what kind of statements they try to show me, I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. I just know what's really going on.
